1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Time plan and method. Which layer solves it. Numbers to memorize. Look-alike pairs. Five questions for every scenario. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All domains: time plan, chooser tables, look-alike terms and decision rules. Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Time plan and method
1.text: Time plan and method. The exam lasts one hundred minutes, and you need seven hundred on a scale to one thousand to pass. It is proctored. The study guide says it may include interactive components, so do not assume every item is multiple choice. Plan by minutes, not by item count.

1.title: Time plan and method, continued
1.text: Time plan and method. Settle. Minutes: About five. What to do: Read the instructions; note any interactive components. First pass. Minutes: About sixty-five. What to do: Answer what you know; if an item is unclear after about two minutes, mark it and move on. Second pass. Minutes: About twenty-five. What to do: Return to the marked items and use the five questions in section five. Final check. Minutes: About five. What to do: Make sure nothing is unanswered; reread words such as "first" and "least". The method for every item has four steps. Read the last sentence first. It says what to deliver: a feature, a first step or a result.

1.title: Time plan and method, continued
1.text: Time plan and method. Read the scenario and underline the requirements: storage mode, license, who the user is, what must not change. Cross out every option that breaks one requirement. Pick the simplest built-in feature that meets all of them. Exam tip: Mark and return: if you cannot decide in about two minutes, give your best answer, mark the item and move on. An unanswered item can never score.

1.title: Which layer solves it
1.text: Which layer solves it. Most scenario questions are really "which layer?" in disguise. Power Query. Choose it when: Data must be cleaned or shaped before it loads. Typical tools: Data types, remove rows and columns, pivot and unpivot, merge and append, parameters, privacy levels. Model. Choose it when: The problem is tables, relationships or properties. Typical tools: Star schema, cardinality, cross-filter direction, date table, sort by column, R L S roles.

1.title: Which layer solves it, continued
1.text: Which layer solves it. dacks. Choose it when: A value must be calculated and follow filters. Typical tools: Measures, calculate, time intelligence, calculated columns and tables, calculation groups, visual calculations. Report. Choose it when: The problem is what users see and do. Typical tools: Visual choice, formatting, slicers, bookmarks, drillthrough, themes, accessibility, A I visuals, Copilot. Service. Choose it when: The problem is sharing, schedule or security. Typical tools: Workspaces, apps, refresh, gateways, subscriptions, alerts, endorsement, labels, R L S members.

1.title: Which layer solves it, continued
1.text: Which layer solves it. Shape before load, relate in the model, calculate in dacks, show in the report, share and secure in the service. When both work, prefer a Power Query column to a dacks calculated column, because it compresses better. Use a measure when the result must respond to filters. Exam tip: Name the layer before you read the options. If the fix is a ratio that must stay correct at every total, it is a measure, not a column.

1.title: Numbers to memorize
1.text: Numbers to memorize. eight and forty-eight. Scheduled refreshes a day: Pro up to eight; P P U, Premium and Fabric up to forty-eight. one thousand rows. Default for column profiling; switch to the entire data set in the status bar. one million rows. A Direct Query query that returns more than one million rows fails. two hundred fifty characters. Maximum length of alt text. four point five to one. Minimum contrast ratio for text.

1.title: Numbers to memorize, continued
1.text: Numbers to memorize. twenty-four and two hundred fifty. Email subscriptions per item; data alerts. F two or P one. Smallest paid capacity for Copilot: Fabric F two or Premium P one. four failures. Consecutive refresh failures that disable a schedule. one hundred and seven hundred. Exam minutes; passing score on a scale to one thousand. Exam tip: Pro: eight refreshes a day. P P U, Premium, Fabric: forty-eight. Direct Lake and Copilot questions usually hide a capacity requirement: look for Fabric F two or higher, or Premium P one or higher.

1.title: Look-alike pairs
1.text: Look-alike pairs. Prepare and model. Import, Direct Query, Direct Lake. Import copies data into the model; Direct Query queries the source for each visual; Direct Lake reads Delta tables in One Lake on Fabric capacity. Reference and duplicate. Reference starts from another query's output, so changes flow through; duplicate copies the steps as an independent query. Merge and append. Merge adds columns by matching keys; append stacks rows from queries with the same columns. Calculated column and measure. A column is computed per row at refresh and stored; a measure is computed at query time and follows filter context.

1.title: Look-alike pairs, continued
1.text: Look-alike pairs. Visualize and manage. Bookmark and drillthrough. A bookmark saves a view; drillthrough opens a detail page filtered to the chosen data point. Slicer and filter. A slicer is a visual on the page; a filter lives in the Filters pane at visual, page or report level. Viewer and Contributor under R L S. R L S restricts Viewers only; a Contributor sees every row. Promoted and the higher level. Owners can set Promoted; only authorized reviewers set the higher level.

1.title: Look-alike pairs, continued
1.text: Look-alike pairs. App and share. An app is a curated set with audiences, one per workspace; a share link gives one item, Read by default. Dashboard and report. A dashboard is one page of tiles built in the service; a report has pages, slicers and filters. Personal and standard gateway. Personal: one user, Import refresh only; standard: shared, supports Direct Query and live connection. Exam tip: Under R L S only the Viewer role is restricted. Pair it with "Promoted is owner-set, the higher level is reviewer-set" and "one app per workspace" to settle most Manage questions.

2.title: Five questions for every scenario
2.text: Five questions for every scenario. What exactly is asked? A feature, a first step or a result. Which layer owns the problem? Power Query, model, dacks, report or service. Which facts limit the choice? Storage mode, license or capacity, where the source is, the user's role. Which options fail a requirement? Cross them out. Which option is the simplest built-in feature? Choose the least effort that meets every requirement.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A retailer's fact table has hundreds of millions of rows in a Fabric lakehouse. Users need near current data and fast visuals without a long refresh. Which storage mode fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Direct Lake on the lakehouse Delta tables. Direct Lake reads Delta tables in One Lake, its refresh copies only metadata, and visuals run on the Verti Paq engine like Import.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A finance team's model must show profit margin that stays correct at every level when users slice by Region or Product. What should the modeler create? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A dacks measure that divides total profit by total sales. A measure is calculated at query time in the current filter context, so the ratio is correct at every total, while a per-row column is not.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Users of a regional sales page must right-click a region and jump to a detail page that is already filtered to that region. Which feature should you configure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A drillthrough page with the region field. Drillthrough opens a detail page filtered to the chosen data point, while a bookmark only restores a saved view.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A department wants three hundred colleagues to open a curated set of reports and dashboards, with different content for two groups. What should an Admin use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A workspace app with two audiences. An app delivers curated content, and audiences control which content each group sees.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. An analyst has twelve monthly files with identical columns and needs one table that holds all rows. Which transformation should the analyst use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Append the queries into one table. Append stacks the rows of queries that have the same columns, whereas merge adds columns by matching keys.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. During the exam you cannot choose between two options after about two minutes. What should you do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Pick your best answer, mark the item and come back. Marking the item with a best answer protects your score and saves minutes for the rest.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How long is the exam, and what score passes? Answer: one hundred minutes; seven hundred on a scale to one thousand. Question two. How many scheduled refreshes a day do Pro and Premium allow? Answer: Pro up to eight; P P U, Premium and Fabric up to forty-eight. Question three. What happens to a Direct Query query that returns more than one million rows? Answer: It fails.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the maximum length of alt text? Answer: two hundred fifty characters. Question five. What is the minimum contrast ratio for text? Answer: four point five to one. Question six. What is the smallest paid capacity that supports Copilot? Answer: Fabric F two or Premium P one.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Time plan: one hundred minutes: about five settle, sixty-five first pass, twenty-five second pass, five final check. Method: read the last sentence first; underline requirements; cross out; pick the simplest built-in feature. Layers: Power Query shapes; model relates; dacks calculates; report shows; service shares and secures. Refresh and limits: eight or forty-eight refreshes; one thousand profiling rows; one million Direct Query rows. Accessibility and sharing: two hundred fifty characters alt text; four point five to one contrast; twenty-four subscriptions; two hundred fifty alerts. Capacity and score: Copilot needs F two or P one; one hundred minutes; seven hundred to pass. Look-alikes: Viewer only under R L S; Promoted versus the higher level; app versus share. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
